title: Uneven token velocity causing slab blocking and intermittent tail latency
creator: Maya Patel
description: Summary: During a production capacity window on 2026-02-28 we observed repeated intermittent tail-latency spikes (~P99.9) for a subset of text-generation customers. The spikes correlated with prolonged batch formation delays for medium-length requests (200-600 tokens) coming from a small set of clients sending bursts with highly variable token velocity. Investigation showed a KV-cache slab allocator path that took a global mutex while initializing cold slabs; requests that needed cold-slab allocation could hold the allocator long enough to block batch assembly and amplify tail latency for colocated requests. This ticket tracks the post-incident analysis and remediation plan.
timeline: 2026-02-28 02:14 UTC: Alerting detected P99.9 latency > 4s on serving region us-west-2
2026-02-28 02:17 UTC: On-call routed to batching and runtime owners; mitigation toggle applied to reduce batch window for impacted pools
2026-02-28 02:45 UTC: Temporary fallback to smaller model variant for highest-latency traffic to restore SLOs
2026-03-01 10:00 UTC: Core dump + flamegraphs captured for an affected host; KV-cache allocator hotspots identified
2026-03-03 16:30 UTC: Reproduced slab allocation stall in integration harness using synthetic token-velocity trace
2026-03-09 09:00 UTC: Design review for long-term allocator fix and batching isolation approaches
root_causes: KV-cache slab allocator took a global mutex during cold-slab initialization leading to pauses in the hot path

Highly skewed token velocity from a small cohort of clients caused uneven progress within the continuous batcher (some requests produced tokens much faster than others), increasing the probability that slab allocation coincided with active batch assembly
Batcher fairness heuristics did not isolate slow-path allocation stalls from priority lanes; a single cold-slab event could stall multiple priority groups
Insufficient observability for cold-slab allocation frequency and mutex hold times made detection and triage slower
mitigations_taken: Rolled out a short-term config: force per-request pre-warm of KV-cache entries for models with known cold-start patterns
Lowered max batch window to 5ms for affected customer pools to reduce amplification while retaining throughput for other pools
Deployed a runtime flag to skip heavy-synchronous slab init on hot request path, falling back to async background warm-up
Added temporary alert rule for KV allocator mutex hold > 2ms per request
decision_log: 2026-03-03: Agreed to avoid a risky global allocator rewrite in the short-term; prefer an incremental approach with async pre-warm and per-shard allocators
2026-03-05: PM approved rollout of async slab init flag behind a kill switch and per-customer opt-in for aggressive pre-warm
2026-03-09: Prioritized changes that reduce customer-visible latency first, deferring full allocator refactor to a follow-up release

(A3) Instrument allocator: emit metrics for cold-slab inits, mutex hold time, and per-shard allocation counts. Owner: Samir Khan. Estimate: 2. Due: 2026-03-10 (done)
(A4) Create an automatic mitigation: if cold-slab events cross threshold, automatically reduce batch window only for affected pool for 1 minute. Owner: Lena Morales. Estimate: 3. Due: 2026-03-18
(A5) Postmortem write-up and customer comms: coordinate with Customer Success for impacted customers and prepare RCA summary. Owner: Maya Patel. Estimate: 1. Due: 2026-03-12 (done)
(A6) Long-term: full allocator refactor to remove sync path from request hot loop; schedule as runtime-1.21 epic. Owner: Runtime team lead. Estimate: 20. Due: 2026-05-15

review_feedback: Security review: no customer-facing secrets touched; security team ok with async init but requested thorough testing under multi-tenant load

Observability: request explicit histograms for allocator hold times by model and pool
